subproblem.title: Allard's Lemma 8.5.10 in corrected form 5.10′ with Remark 5.11: bad-set and fibre-density bounds
subproblem.statement: Assume MonotonicityFormula (Simon 8.3.3, frozen contract statement). Let N, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1 and Λ ≥ 1. There are δ̄ > 0 and c₀ ≥ 0 such that for all δ ∈ (0,δ̄] and ε ∈ (0,δ⁴], every U ⊆ ℝ^N with B°_3(0) ⊆ U, every n-varifold W on U with locally bounded first variation and every P ∈ G(N,n) with (‡) μ_W(B°_3(0)) ≤ Λ, ‖δW‖(B°_3(0)) < ε² and ∫_{B°_3(0)×G} t_P(S) dW(z,S) < ε² (t_P(S) the operator norm of p_S − p_P): calling y good if (1) ‖δW‖(B_ρ(y)) ≤ εμ_W(B_ρ(y)) for all ρ ∈ (0,1) and (2) ∫_{B_ρ(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ερ^n for all ρ ∈ (0,1), (a) the set E of points of B_2(0) ∩ spt μ_W that are not good has μ_W(E) ≤ c₀ε; (b) for every x ∈ P with |x| < 1, every finite set s of good points y ∈ B_2(0) ∩ spt μ_W with p_P(y) = x and |y − p_P(y)| < ε, and every Θ : ℝ^N → [0,∞] with HasDensity n μ_W y (Θ(y)) and Θ(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ s: Σ_{y∈s} Θ(y) ≤ (1+δ)μ_W(B_1(x))/ω_n + δ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 8.5.10, Remark 5.11 and the printed proof of 5.10 (pp. 219–223), in the corrected form of step B5 of the parent proof. ERRATA (E2): in (1), "δ‖W‖(B_ρ(y))" means ‖δW‖(B_ρ(y)); (6)–(7) are stated for y ∈ B_1^n(0) ∖ p(A_1 ∪ A_2) but are used, and proved, for good points y of spt μ; the sign of δV(X) in 3.5 is "−" (SimonGMT WeightedRadialIdentity.lean), irrelevant because only |δW(X)| enters; the normalisation "translating and changing scale by 3/2" is replaced by working directly with balls of radius 1 at every fibre. Integrality of W is not used. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; μ := μ_W = W.weight; ‖δW‖ := variationMeasure W; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞), also used for its real value; Θ^n(μ,y) = c means HasDensity n μ y c; p := Grassmannian.project P, q := id − p (|v|² = |pv|² + |qv|², q symmetric idempotent); t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖, the operator norm of p_S − p, so |(p_S − p)v| ≤ t_P(S)|v|; U^τ_σ(y) := B_σ(y) ∩ {z : |q(z − y)| < τ} (Borel). "y satisfies (1)" means ‖δW‖(B_ρ(y)) ≤ ε μ(B_ρ(y)) for all ρ ∈ (0,1); "y satisfies (2)" means ∫_{B_ρ(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ερ^n for all ρ ∈ (0,1); E := {y ∈ B_2(0) ∩ spt μ : not ((1) and (2))}. N_B = N_B(N) is the Besicovitch constant of ℝ^N. Constants: c1 := eΛ/ω_n, c0 := N_B(c1ω_n + 1) = N_B(eΛ + 1), c3 := 2^{n+1}(4 + c1ω_n), c2 := c3/ω_n (they depend only on n, N, Λ); δ̄ ∈ (0,1/2] is fixed in step 7 and depends only on n, N, Λ. Throughout, δ ∈ (0,δ̄] and ε ∈ (0,δ⁴], so ε ≤ 1/16 and e^ε ≤ 2; U ⊇ B°_3(0), W, P satisfy the hypotheses (LBFV and (‡)).

1. Monotonicity at points satisfying (1) (printed (3)). Let y ∈ B_2(0) satisfy (1). Then B°_1(y) ⊆ B°_3(0) ⊆ U, and the hypothesis MonotonicityFormula applied to W, y, ρ₀ := 1 and Λ_mono := ε gives: ρ ↦ e^{ερ}μ(B_ρ(y))/ρ^n is non-decreasing on (0,1); Θ^n(μ,y) exists and is finite; Θ^n(μ,y) ≤ e^{εσ}μ(B_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) for σ ∈ (0,1). For 0 < σ ≤ ρ < 1, e^{εσ}μ(B_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ e^{ερ}μ(B_ρ(y))/ρ^n ≤ e^ε Λ/ρ^n (B_ρ(y) ⊆ B°_3(0), μ(B°_3(0)) ≤ Λ); letting ρ ↑ 1, μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^εΛσ^n ≤ c1ω_nσ^n for every σ ∈ (0,1).

2. The bad set (printed (4)–(5)); proof of (a). Let A_1 := {y ∈ E : (1) fails}. For y ∈ A_1 choose ρ_y ∈ (0,1) with ε μ(B_{ρ_y}(y)) < ‖δW‖(B_{ρ_y}(y)). For y ∈ E ∖ A_1, (1) holds and (2) fails, so by step 1 there is ρ_y ∈ (0,1) with ∫_{B_{ρ_y}(y)×G} t_P dW > ερ_y^n ≥ (ε/(c1ω_n)) μ(B_{ρ_y}(y)). In both cases μ(B_{ρ_y}(y)) ≤ (c1ω_n/ε)∫_{B_{ρ_y}(y)×G} t_P dW + ε^{-1}‖δW‖(B_{ρ_y}(y)), and B_{ρ_y}(y) ⊆ B°_3(0) (|y| ≤ 2, ρ_y < 1). By the Besicovitch covering theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.12; Mathlib Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families, or SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_besicovitchCovering_families after importing it) the balls B_{ρ_y}(y), y ∈ E, contain N_B subfamilies, each pairwise disjoint (hence countable: Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior), whose union covers E. For one such disjoint subfamily 𝓑, summing over its balls (disjoint subsets of B°_3(0)): Σ_{B∈𝓑} μ(B) ≤ (c1ω_n/ε)∫_{B°_3(0)×G} t_P dW + ε^{-1}‖δW‖(B°_3(0)) < (c1ω_n/ε)ε² + ε^{-1}ε² = (c1ω_n + 1)ε by (‡). Hence μ(E) ≤ N_B(c1ω_n + 1)ε = c0ε (outer measure; E need not be measurable). This is (a), for every δ, ε as above.

3. Cylinder monotonicity (printed (7)). Claim: if y ∈ B_2(0) satisfies (1) and (2), 0 < τ ≤ 1 and 0 < σ ≤ ρ < 1, then μ(U^τ_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) ≤ μ(U^{2τ}_ρ(y))/(ω_nρ^n) + c2ερ/τ.
 Proof. Choose a C^∞ non-increasing f : ℝ → [0,1] with f = 1 on (−∞,τ], f = 0 on [2τ,∞) and |f'| ≤ 4/τ (e.g. a rescaled Real.smoothTransition, whose derivative is at most 2/τ), and set h(z) := f(|q(z − y)|). As f is constant near 0, h is C¹ with 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, ∇h(z) = f'(|q(z − y)|) q(z − y)/|q(z − y)| ∈ P^⊥ and |∇h| ≤ 4/τ; hence p∇h = 0 and |p_S∇h| = |(p_S − p)∇h| ≤ (4/τ)t_P(S) for S ∈ G. Fix η₀ ∈ (0,1] with (1+η₀)ρ < 1; for each η ∈ (0,η₀] fix a C¹ non-increasing φ_η : ℝ → [0,1] with φ_η = 1 on (−∞,1] and φ_η = 0 on [(1+η)²,∞); and let R := ((1+η₀)ρ + 1)/2 < 1, so B_R(y) ⊆ B°_3(0) ⊆ U and t(1+η) < R for t ∈ [σ,ρ]. Let Ĩ(t) := ∫ φ_η(|z − y|²/t²) h(z) dμ(z) (= Varifold.weightedCutoffMass W y h φ_η t). By the weighted radial identity 3.5 (SimonGMT Varifold.hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.WeightedRadialIdentity, which the prover may need to import; centre y, A := 1 + η, this R; valid at every t ∈ [σ,ρ] since t(1+η) < R), d/dt(t^{-n}Ĩ(t)) = t^{-n}J̃'(t) + t^{-n-1}(G(t) − δW(X_t)), where J̃'(t) = ∫ (−2|z−y|²/t³) φ_η'(|z−y|²/t²) · (radialNormalSq) · h(z) dW ≥ 0 (φ_η' ≤ 0, h ≥ 0, radialNormalSq ≥ 0; it is the derivative of Varifold.weightedCutoffNormalMass), X_t(z) := h(z) φ_η(|z−y|²/t²)(z − y) (weightedRadialVectorField) and G(t) := ∫ φ_η(|z−y|²/t²) ⟨∇h(z), p_S(z − y)⟩ dW(z,S) (weightedRadialGradientTerm). X_t is a C¹ test field on U with tsupport X_t ⊆ B_{(1+η)t}(y) and |X_t| ≤ (1+η)t, so by the polar representation of δW (SimonGMT Varifold.isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz; ‖δW‖ = variationMeasure W since W has LBFV), (1) and step 1: |δW(X_t)| ≤ (1+η)t ‖δW‖(B_{(1+η)t}(y)) ≤ (1+η)t ε μ(B_{(1+η)t}(y)) ≤ (1+η)^{n+1} ε c1ω_n t^{n+1}. Since ⟨∇h, p_S(z − y)⟩ = ⟨p_S∇h, z − y⟩, (2) gives |G(t)| ≤ (1+η)t(4/τ)∫_{B_{(1+η)t}(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ 4(1+η)^{n+1}εt^{n+1}/τ. Hence, as η ≤ 1 and τ ≤ 1, d/dt(t^{-n}Ĩ(t)) ≥ −(1+η)^{n+1}ε(4/τ + c1ω_n) ≥ −c3ε/τ on [σ,ρ], and by the mean value theorem ρ^{-n}Ĩ(ρ) − σ^{-n}Ĩ(σ) ≥ −c3ε(ρ − σ)/τ ≥ −c3ερ/τ. Let η ↓ 0 along η = η₀/j: φ_η(|z−y|²/t²) → 1_{B_t(y)}(z) for every z (φ_η = 1 on (−∞,1] and = 0 on [(1+η)²,∞)), dominated by 1_{B_{(1+η₀)t}(y)}, and B_{(1+η₀)t}(y) is a compact subset of B°_3(0) with μ-measure ≤ Λ; so Ĩ(t) → ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ by dominated convergence (no monotonicity in η is needed). Thus σ^{-n}∫_{B_σ(y)} h dμ ≤ ρ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ(y)} h dμ + c3ερ/τ. Finally U^τ_σ(y) ⊆ {h = 1} ∩ B_σ(y) and {h > 0} ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ U^{2τ}_ρ(y), so μ(U^τ_σ(y))/σ^n ≤ μ(U^{2τ}_ρ(y))/ρ^n + c3ερ/τ; divide by ω_n.

4. Density bound by cylinders (printed (6)). Claim: if y ∈ B_2(0) satisfies (1) and (2), 0 < τ ≤ 1/4 and 0 < σ < 1, then Θ^n(μ,y) ≤ e^ε μ(U^{4τ}_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) + c2εσ/τ. If τ ≥ σ: B_σ(y) ⊆ U^{4τ}_σ(y) (|q(z−y)| ≤ |z−y| ≤ σ < 4τ), and step 1 gives Θ^n(μ,y) ≤ e^{εσ}μ(B_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) ≤ e^εμ(U^{4τ}_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n). If τ < σ: step 1 gives Θ^n(μ,y) ≤ e^{ετ}μ(B_τ(y))/(ω_nτ^n), B_τ(y) ⊆ U^{2τ}_τ(y), and step 3 with parameter 2τ ≤ 1/2 and radii τ < σ gives μ(U^{2τ}_τ(y))/(ω_nτ^n) ≤ μ(U^{4τ}_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) + c2εσ/(2τ); since e^ε ≤ 2, Θ^n(μ,y) ≤ e^εμ(U^{4τ}_σ(y))/(ω_nσ^n) + c2εσ/τ.

5. Clustering (printed (8)). Call y_1, …, y_m (m ≥ 1) admissible at x if x ∈ P.plane, |x| < 1, the y_j are distinct, p(y_j) = x, |q(y_j)| < ε, and every y_j lies in B_2(0) and satisfies (1) and (2). Then y_j − y_l = q(y_j) − q(y_l) and |y_j − x| = |q(y_j)| < ε. Claim: for every m ≥ 1 there are c_m ≥ 1 and δ_m ∈ (0,1/2] (depending only on n, N, Λ, m) such that for δ ∈ (0,δ_m], ε ∈ (0,δ⁴] and y_1,…,y_m admissible at x: if m = 1, μ(U^τ_σ(y_1))/(ω_nσ^n) ≤ (1 + c_1δ²)μ(B_1(x))/ω_n for all τ > 0 and 0 < σ ≤ 1 − ε; if m ≥ 2, with d := min_{j≠l}|y_j − y_l| ∈ (0,2ε), for all σ, τ > 0 with 2δ²σ ≤ τ ≤ d/4: Σ_j μ(U^τ_σ(y_j))/(ω_nσ^n) ≤ (1 + c_mδ²)μ(B_1(x))/ω_n + c_mδ². Proof by strong induction on m.
 m = 1: μ(U^τ_σ(y_1)) ≤ μ(B_σ(y_1)); by step 1 (σ ≤ 1 − ε < 1), μ(B_σ(y_1))/σ^n ≤ e^{ε(1−ε)}μ(B_{1−ε}(y_1))/(1−ε)^n ≤ e^ε(1−ε)^{-n}μ(B_1(x)), as B_{1−ε}(y_1) ⊆ B_1(x). Since ε ≤ δ⁴ ≤ δ², e^ε(1−ε)^{-n} ≤ 1 + c_1δ² for a suitable c_1 = c_1(n) and all δ ≤ δ_1 (small).
 m ≥ 2: let ρ := d/(4δ²) and τ̃ := 2δ²ρ = d/2. Then σ ≤ τ/(2δ²) ≤ d/(8δ²) < ρ < ε/(2δ²) ≤ δ²/2 < 1.
 (a) Since τ ≤ d/4 = τ̃/2, U^τ_σ(y_j) ⊆ U^{τ̃/2}_σ(y_j), and step 3 with parameter τ̃/2 ≤ 1 gives μ(U^τ_σ(y_j))/(ω_nσ^n) ≤ μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j))/(ω_nρ^n) + c2ερ/(τ̃/2) = μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j))/(ω_nρ^n) + c2ε/δ² ≤ μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j))/(ω_nρ^n) + c2δ².
 (b) The sets U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j) (j = 1,…,m) are pairwise disjoint: a common point z would give |y_j − y_l| = |q(y_j) − q(y_l)| ≤ |q(z − y_j)| + |q(z − y_l)| < 2τ̃ = d.
 (c) For t > 0 let 𝒞(t) be the partition of {1,…,m} into the connected components of the graph joining j and l when |y_j − y_l| ≤ t. #𝒞(d) ≤ m − 1, and t ↦ #𝒞(t) is non-increasing with values in {1,…,m−1} for t ≥ d. With t_i := (10m)^i d (i = 0,…,m−1), the m values #𝒞(t_0) ≥ … ≥ #𝒞(t_{m−1}) lie in a set with m − 1 elements, so #𝒞(t_i) = #𝒞(t_{i+1}) for some i ≤ m − 2; since 𝒞(t_{i+1}) coarsens 𝒞(t_i), 𝒞(t_i) = 𝒞(t_{i+1}) =: {C_1,…,C_Q} with Q ≤ m − 1. Two indices in one class are joined by a path of at most m − 1 edges of length ≤ t_i, so every class has diameter ≤ s := (m−1)t_i ≤ (10m)^m d; indices in different classes satisfy |y_j − y_l| > t_{i+1} = 10m t_i. Pick z_k ∈ {y_j : j ∈ C_k} and put τ̂ := τ̃ + s and ρ̂ := ρ + s. Then U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j) ⊆ U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z_k) for j ∈ C_k (|z − z_k| ≤ |z − y_j| + |y_j − z_k| and |q(z − z_k)| ≤ |q(z − y_j)| + |y_j − z_k|); ρ̂ ≤ ρ(1 + 4(10m)^mδ²) because s ≤ (10m)^m d = (10m)^m 4δ²ρ; 2δ²ρ̂ = τ̃ + 2δ²s ≤ τ̂; and 4τ̂ = 4(d/2 + s) ≤ 2t_i + 4(m−1)t_i ≤ 10m t_i < min_{k≠k'}|z_k − z_{k'}| =: d' (if Q ≥ 2), i.e. τ̂ ≤ d'/4.
 (d) By (b) and (c), for each k the pairwise disjoint sets U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j), j ∈ C_k, lie in U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z_k); so Σ_j μ(U^{τ̃}_ρ(y_j))/ρ^n ≤ Σ_k μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z_k))/ρ^n = (ρ̂/ρ)^n Σ_k μ(U^{τ̂}_{ρ̂}(z_k))/ρ̂^n.

subproblem.title: Canonical tangent-plane representation and null-set transfer for varifolds with positive density (step B2)
subproblem.statement: Assume AllardRectifiabilityTheorem and FirstRectifiabilityTheorem (frozen contract statements). Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N and V an n-varifold on U with locally bounded first variation such that Θ^n(μ_V, x) exists and is > 0 for μ_V-a.e. x. Let M := {x ∈ spt μ_V : HasTangentPlane V x T θ' for some T ∈ G(N,n), θ' ∈ ℝ}. Then there is θ : ℝ^N → ℝ such that (i) IsVarifoldOf V M θ; (ii) for every x ∈ M there is T with HasTangentPlane V x T (θ(x)), and Θ^n(μ_V, x) = θ(x) (HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ(x))); (iii) every Z ⊆ M with μ_V(Z) = 0 has H^n(Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: AllardRectifiabilityTheorem → FirstRectifiabilityTheorem → ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U), V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, HasDensity n V.weight x θ ∧ 0 < θ) → ∃ θ : Euclidean N → ℝ, IsVarifoldOf V {x | x ∈ V.weight.support ∧ ∃ (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ' : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ'} θ ∧ (∀ x ∈ {x | x ∈ V.weight.support ∧ ∃ (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ' : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}, (∃ T : Grassmannian N n, HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x)) ∧ HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) ∧ ∀ Z ⊆ {x | x ∈ V.weight.support ∧ ∃ (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ' : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}, V.weight Z = 0 → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) Z = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step B2 of the parent proof of Simon 8.5.9 (canonical representation of a varifold with tangent planes a.e., the tangent-point facts from Def. 8.1.1, and Ch. 1 Theorem 3.3); it is used for the limit varifold V and for the blow-ups W_k. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact); μ_V := V.weight; B_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞) (ω_0 = 1); V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t, so ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t^{-n}∫ f(t^{-1}(z − x), S) dV(z,S); v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T; M := {x ∈ spt μ_V : ∃ T θ', HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}.

1. Tangent planes a.e. By the hypothesis AllardRectifiabilityTheorem (its second conclusion) applied to V, which has locally bounded first variation and Θ^n(μ_V, x) > 0 for μ_V-a.e. x: for μ_V-a.e. x there are T ∈ G and θ' ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ'.

2. Canonical representation. By the hypothesis FirstRectifiabilityTheorem applied to V and step 1, there is θ : ℝ^N → ℝ such that every x ∈ M has some T ∈ G with HasTangentPlane V x T (θ(x)), and IsVarifoldOf V M θ. This is (i) and the first half of (ii). In particular M ⊆ U and θ > 0 on M.

3. Tangent-point density fact. Claim: if HasTangentPlane V x T θ_1 (so x ∈ U, θ_1 > 0, and ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ_1 ∫ f dv(T) as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G)), then HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ_1). Proof: for g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) the function f(z,S) := g(z) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G) because G is compact; ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t^{-n}∫ g(t^{-1}(z − x)) dμ_V(z) (definitions of rescaledMeasure and of μ_V = π_#V), and ∫ f dv(T) = ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n. For κ ∈ (0,1) choose continuous g_1, g_2 : ℝ^N → [0,1] with 1_{B_κ(0)} ≤ g_1 ≤ 1_{B_1(0)} ≤ g_2 ≤ 1_{B_{1/κ}(0)}. For t so small that B_{t/κ}(x) is a compact subset of U (x ∈ U, U open), the functions z ↦ g_i(t^{-1}(z−x)) are bounded with support in B_{t/κ}(x), hence μ_V-integrable (μ_V is finite on compact subsets of U), so the Bochner integrals equal the corresponding lintegrals and t^{-n}∫ g_1(t^{-1}(z−x)) dμ_V ≤ t^{-n}μ_V(B_t(x)) ≤ t^{-n}∫ g_2(t^{-1}(z−x)) dμ_V, and H^n(T.plane ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n s^n for s > 0 (T.plane is an n-dimensional subspace, isometric to ℝ^n, on which μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; for n = 0, T.plane = {0}, H^0 is counting measure and ω_0 = 1). Letting t ↓ 0: θ_1 ω_n κ^n ≤ liminf_{t↓0} t^{-n}μ_V(B_t(x)) ≤ limsup_{t↓0} t^{-n}μ_V(B_t(x)) ≤ θ_1 ω_n κ^{-n}. Letting κ ↑ 1 and dividing by ω_n ∈ (0,∞): densityRatio n μ_V x t → θ_1, i.e. HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ_1). Applied with θ_1 := θ(x) for x ∈ M (step 2), this is the second half of (ii).

4. μ_V-null subsets of M are H^n-null. Let Z ⊆ M with μ_V(Z) = 0. If U = ∅ then Z = ∅. Otherwise let K_p (p ∈ ℕ) be compact with K_p ⊆ interior K_{p+1} and ⋃_p K_p = U (U is open), and O_p := interior K_{p+1}, an open set with μ_V(O_p) ≤ μ_V(K_{p+1}) < ∞. Fix p and k ≥ 1 and put Z_{p,k} := {x ∈ Z ∩ K_p : θ(x) ≥ 1/k}; Z_{p,k} ⊆ O_p. Let η > 0. The finite Borel measure μ_V⌞O_p on the metric space ℝ^N is outer regular and (μ_V⌞O_p)(Z_{p,k}) ≤ μ_V(Z) = 0, so there is an open O'' ⊇ Z_{p,k} with μ_V(O'' ∩ O_p) < η; then O := O'' ∩ O_p is open, Z_{p,k} ⊆ O, μ_V(O) < η. For x ∈ Z_{p,k} and 0 < ρ < dist(x, ℝ^N ∖ O) we have (μ_V⌞O)(B_ρ(x)) = μ_V(B_ρ(x)), so by step 3 the upper n-density of the finite measure μ_V⌞O at x equals θ(x) ≥ 1/k. By Simon Ch. 1 Theorem 3.3 (SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3 / mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity, applied to the Borel regular outer measure of μ_V⌞O with A_1 := Z_{p,k} and A_2 := ℝ^N; Simon's Hausdorff measure and density normalisation agree with H^n = μHE[n] and ω_n up to fixed positive finite factors, so it yields C·(1/k)·H^n(Z_{p,k}) ≤ (μ_V⌞O)(ℝ^N) for a constant C = C(n) ∈ (0,∞); in fact C = 1, since simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n] by SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and the outer measure of μ_V⌞O is Borel regular by Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular), we get C(1/k)H^n(Z_{p,k}) ≤ μ_V(O) < η. Since η > 0 is arbitrary, H^n(Z_{p,k}) = 0. As θ > 0 on Z ⊆ M ⊆ U = ⋃_p K_p, Z = ⋃_{p,k} Z_{p,k}, hence H^n(Z) = 0. This is (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: AllardRectifiabilityTheorem gives tangent planes μ_V-a.e.
FirstRectifiabilityTheorem gives θ with IsVarifoldOf V M θ and a tangent plane of multiplicity θ(x) at every x ∈ M.
Tangent-point fact (Def. 8.1.1 tested with radial cut-offs, H^n(T ∩ B_s) = ω_n s^n): HasTangentPlane V x T θ₁ ⇒ Θ^n(μ_V,x) = θ₁.
Null transfer: for Z ⊆ M μ_V-null, outer regularity gives small open O ⊇ Z_{p,k}, and Ch. 1 Theorem 3.3 gives (1/k)H^n(Z_{p,k}) ≲ μ_V(O); hence H^n(Z) = 0.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure on small-slope Lipschitz graphs is bounded by fibre sums over the base plane
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n) with orthogonal projection p and q := id − p, L ≥ 0, Γ_i ⊆ ℝ^N (i ∈ ℕ) closed sets each an L-Lipschitz graph over P (|q(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for y, z ∈ Γ_i), G ⊆ ⋃_i Γ_i an H^n-null-measurable set and g : ℝ^N → [0,∞] arbitrary. Then ∫⁻_G g dH^n ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} ∫⁻_{P} (Σ_{y∈G, p(y)=a} g(y)) dH^n(a), the inner sum being the [0,∞]-valued sum over the fibre {y ∈ G : p(y) = a}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (L : ℝ) (Γ : ℕ → Set (Euclidean N)) (G : Set (Euclidean N)) (g : Euclidean N → ℝ≥0∞), 0 ≤ L → (∀ i, IsClosed (Γ i)) → (∀ i, ∀ y ∈ Γ i, ∀ z ∈ Γ i, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) → G ⊆ ⋃ i, Γ i → NullMeasurableSet G (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → ∫⁻ y in G, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + L ^ 2) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) * ∫⁻ a in (P.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), (∑' y : {y : Euclidean N // y ∈ G ∧ Grassmannian.project P y = a}, g y) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the parent proof of Simon 8.5.9 (the graph inequality that replaces the area formula on rectifiable carriers). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; p := Grassmannian.project P (orthogonal projection onto P.plane: linear, symmetric, idempotent, |p v| ≤ |v|), q := id − p, |v|² = |p v|² + |q v|²; for a ∈ ℝ^N the fibre sum is Σ_{y∈G, p(y)=a} u(y) := the [0,∞]-valued sum (tsum) of u over the subtype {y ∈ G : p(y) = a}.

2. Transfer of measurability and of null sets. Let B ⊆ Γ_i. If B is Borel, then p(B) = {a ∈ p(Γ_i) : h_i(a) ∈ B} is Borel (h_i is continuous on the closed set p(Γ_i), so this is the preimage of a Borel set under a continuous map on a closed, hence Borel, domain). Hence, if B is H^n-null-measurable, so is p(B): write B = B_1 ∪ Y with B_1 Borel, B_1 ⊆ Γ_i and H^n(Y) = 0 (intersect a Borel/null decomposition of B with the closed set Γ_i), so p(B) = p(B_1) ∪ p(Y).

Extend h_i to all of ℝ^N by h_i := Function.invFunOn p Γ_i (so h_i(p(y)) = y for y ∈ Γ_i) and let s_i := 1_{p(A_i)}·(s∘h_i). Because p is injective on Γ_i ⊇ A_i, for a ∈ p(A_i) we have 1_{E_j}(h_i(a)) = 1_{p(A_i ∩ E_j)}(a), so s_i = Σ_j c_j·1_{p(A_i ∩ E_j)}; in particular s_i is H^n-a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.indicator₀ / lintegral_indicator_const₀) and vanishes off p(A_i) ⊆ P.plane. The lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻_G g dH^n is the supremum of ∫⁻_G s dH^n over Borel simple functions s ≤ g (definition of MeasureTheory.lintegral and SimpleFunc.lintegral_eq_lintegral, for the measure H^n⌞G). Taking the supremum over s proves ∫⁻_G g dH^n ≤ ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}) · ∫⁻_{P.plane} Σ_{y∈G, p(y)=a} g(y) dH^n(a). ∎

subproblem.title: Integral varifolds have integer density ≥ 1 almost everywhere (step B0)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N and V an n-varifold on U (so U is open). If V is integral (IsIntegral V: IsVarifoldOf V M θ for some M, θ with θ(x) ∈ ℕ for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M), then for μ_V-almost every x there is an integer k ≥ 1 such that the n-dimensional density Θ^n(μ_V, x) exists and equals k (HasDensity n μ_V x k).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U), IsIntegral V → ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ HasDensity n V.weight x (k : ℝ≥0∞)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 8, Remark 5.9 ("the hypothesis Θ^n(μ_{V_j},x) ≥ 1 on U ∖ A_j is automatically satisfied with μ_{V_j}(A_j) = 0"), proved with Ch. 3 Remark 1.8(2) and the upper density theorem Ch. 1, 3.6. This is step B0 of the parent proof of 5.9, for one integral varifold. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; μ_V := V.weight; B_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞) (ω_0 = 1); Θ^n(μ,x) = c means HasDensity n μ x c, i.e. μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → c as ρ ↓ 0.

1. Data. By IsIntegral V choose M, θ with IsVarifoldOf V M θ and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for (H^n⌞M)-a.e. x. Thus M ⊆ U is H^n-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, and for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G: V(A) = ∫⁻ over {x ∈ M : ∃ S ∈ G, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane ∧ (x,S) ∈ A} of ofReal θ dH^n. U is open (Varifold.isOpen_domain). If U = ∅ then μ_V(ℝ^N) = V(U^c × G) = 0 and there is nothing to prove; otherwise fix compact K_p ⊆ U (p ∈ ℕ) with K_p ⊆ interior K_{p+1} and ⋃_p K_p = U. Put M* := {x ∈ M : ∃ S ∈ G, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane} and ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal θ), so ν(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dH^n for Borel B and ν(K_p) < ∞.

2. H^n⌞M is σ-finite. For each p choose a Borel θ_p equal to θ H^n-a.e. on M ∩ K_p (θ is a.e.-strongly measurable there) and a Borel H^n-null Z_p ⊇ {x ∈ M ∩ K_p : θ(x) ≠ θ_p(x)}. The Borel sets U^c, Z_p, K_p ∩ {θ_p ≤ 0} and S_{p,k} := K_p ∩ {θ_p ≥ 1/k} (p ∈ ℕ, k ≥ 1) cover ℝ^N, and (H^n⌞M)(U^c) = 0 (M ⊆ U), (H^n⌞M)(Z_p) = 0, (H^n⌞M)(K_p ∩ {θ_p ≤ 0}) ≤ H^n(Z_p) = 0 (θ_p = θ > 0 on (M ∩ K_p) ∖ Z_p), (H^n⌞M)(S_{p,k}) ≤ k ∫_{M∩K_p} θ dH^n < ∞. Hence H^n⌞M is σ-finite, in particular s-finite.

3. Measurable hull of M*. Let M' := M ∩ toMeasurable_{H^n⌞M}(M*). Then M* ⊆ M' ⊆ M, M' is H^n-null-measurable, and (Measure.restrict_toMeasurable_of_sFinite, Measure.measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite, for the s-finite measure H^n⌞M) (H^n⌞M)⌞M' = (H^n⌞M)⌞M*; in particular H^n(B ∩ M') = H^n(B ∩ M*) (outer measure on the right) for every Borel B. Taking A = B × G (B Borel) in the defining identity: μ_V(B) = V(B × G) = ∫⁻_{M*∩B} θ dH^n = ∫⁻_B θ d((H^n⌞M)⌞M*) = ∫⁻_B θ d((H^n⌞M)⌞M') = ν(B ∩ M') (H^n⌞(M*∩B) = ((H^n⌞M)⌞M*)⌞B by Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset, which needs no measurability, and Measure.restrict_restrict for the Borel set B). Choose a Borel M'_B ⊆ M' with H^n(M' ∖ M'_B) = 0; then μ_V(ℝ^N ∖ M'_B) = ν((ℝ^N ∖ M'_B) ∩ M') = 0 (ν ≪ H^n), so μ_V is carried by the Borel set M'_B; and μ_V(Y) = 0 for every H^n-null Y (μ_V ≤ ν ≪ H^n, applied to a Borel H^n-null superset of Y).

4. Density of ν at approximate tangent points (Ch. 3 Remark 1.8(2)). Let x ∈ M* with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P (P = S.plane, dim P = n): for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dH^n(y) → θ(x) ∫_P f dH^n as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z − x) (blowUpMap). Since H^n(x + rA) = r^n H^n(A) for all A (translation invariance and Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ / euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), the left side equals r^{-n} ∫_M f(r^{-1}(z − x)) θ(z) dH^n(z): for an arbitrary set M one has H^n⌞η_{x,r}(M) = r^{-n}·(η_{x,r})_#(H^n⌞M) as measures (on Borel B both sides equal H^n(B ∩ η_{x,r}(M)) = r^{-n}H^n(η_{x,r}^{-1}(B) ∩ M)), and one applies MeasureTheory.lintegral_map_equiv / integral_map_equiv for the measurable equivalence η_{x,r}. For κ ∈ (0,1) choose continuous f_1, f_2 : ℝ^N → [0,1] with 1_{B_κ(0)} ≤ f_1 ≤ 1_{B_1(0)} ≤ f_2 ≤ 1_{B_{1/κ}(0)}. Let p be such that x ∈ K_p; for r so small that B_{r/κ}(x) ⊆ K_{p+1}, the functions z ↦ f_i(r^{-1}(z−x))θ(z) are H^n-integrable on M (bounded by θ·1_{M∩K_{p+1}}, θ ≥ 0 a.e.-strongly measurable and integrable there), so the Bochner integrals in Definition 1.7 coincide with the corresponding lintegrals and r^{-n}∫_M f_1(r^{-1}(z−x))θ dH^n ≤ r^{-n}ν(B_r(x)) ≤ r^{-n}∫_M f_2(r^{-1}(z−x))θ dH^n, and H^n(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n s^n (P is isometric to ℝ^n, on which μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; for n = 0, P = {0}, H^0 is counting measure and ω_0 = 1). Hence θ(x) ω_n κ^n ≤ liminf_{r↓0} r^{-n}ν(B_r(x)) ≤ limsup_{r↓0} r^{-n}ν(B_r(x)) ≤ θ(x) ω_n κ^{-n}; letting κ ↑ 1, ν(B_r(x))/(ω_n r^n) → θ(x).

5. M ∖ M' has zero density at H^n-a.e. point of M' (Ch. 1, 3.6). Fix p. ν_p := ν⌞K_{p+1} is a finite Borel measure and A_p := (M ∖ M') ∩ K_{p+1} is ν_p-null-measurable (M, M' are H^n-null-measurable and ν ≪ H^n), hence Carathéodory measurable for the outer measure of ν_p (split any test set with Mathlib measure_inter_add_sdiff₀), and ν_p(A_p) < ∞. By the upper density theorem (SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 for the outer measure of ν_p, which is Borel regular by SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular; its Hausdorff measure is Simon's simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, equal to μHE[n] by SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, and its density quotient uses realUnitBallVolume n and rpow, which agree with ω_n and ρ^n for ρ > 0 up to at most a fixed positive finite factor, irrelevant for zero densities), for H^n-a.e. x ∉ A_p: limsup_{ρ↓0} ν_p(A_p ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) = 0. For x ∈ M' ∩ K_p (so x ∉ A_p) and small ρ, B_ρ(x) ⊆ K_{p+1}, hence ν((M∖M') ∩ B_ρ(x)) = ν_p(A_p ∩ B_ρ(x)). Taking the union over p of the exceptional sets: for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M', limsup_{ρ↓0} ν((M ∖ M') ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) = 0.

6. Integer values. Since θ > 0 on M and θ ∈ ℕ (H^n⌞M)-a.e. (M null-measurable), θ(x) ∈ {1,2,3,…} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M. Let N_0 be the H^n-null set of points x ∈ M* at which the conclusion of step 5 or this property fails.

7. Pointwise density. Let x ∈ M* ∖ N_0 and p with x ∈ K_p. For small ρ > 0, B_ρ(x) ⊆ K_{p+1}, all quantities below are finite, and, because ν is carried by M ⊇ M' and M' is ν-null-measurable, μ_V(B_ρ(x)) = ν(B_ρ(x) ∩ M') = ν(B_ρ(x)) − ν((M ∖ M') ∩ B_ρ(x)). Dividing by ω_nρ^n and using steps 4 and 5, μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) = m with m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1; i.e. HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ(x)) and θ(x) ∈ {1,2,…}.

8. Measurability of the exceptional set. Let F := {x ∈ U : ¬(HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ(x)) ∧ ∃ m ∈ ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧ θ(x) = m)} and F_p := F ∩ K_p. For x ∈ K_p and small ρ the density ratios of μ_V and of the finite measure μ_p := μ_V⌞interior(K_{p+1}) coincide, and in [0,∞] the ratio tends to c iff its limsup and liminf as ρ ↓ 0 both equal c. The upper and lower densities of the finite Borel measure μ_p are Borel functions of x (SimonGMT Chapter01.measurable_dimensionalUpperDensity / measurable_dimensionalLowerDensity; their normalising constant differs from ω_n by a fixed positive finite factor), and θ = θ_p H^n-a.e. on M ∩ K_p with θ_p Borel (step 2). Choose also a Borel M_B ⊆ M with H^n(M ∖ M_B) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then F_p ∩ M_B ∩ {θ = θ_p} is the intersection of M_B ∩ K_p with a set defined by Borel conditions on x, up to the H^n-null set Z_p; therefore F_p ∩ M = B_p ∪ Y_p with B_p ⊆ F_p ∩ M Borel and H^n(Y_p) = 0 (Y_p ⊆ (M ∖ M_B) ∪ Z_p).

9. Conclusion. By step 7, F ∩ M* ⊆ N_0. For each p: μ_V(F_p) ≤ μ_V(F_p ∩ M'_B) (μ_V is carried by M'_B, step 3) ≤ μ_V(B_p ∩ M'_B) + μ_V(Y_p) (because F_p ∩ M'_B ⊆ F_p ∩ M = B_p ∪ Y_p), and μ_V(Y_p) = 0 by step 3. As B_p ∩ M'_B is Borel, μ_V(B_p ∩ M'_B) = ∫⁻_{B_p ∩ M'_B} θ d((H^n⌞M)⌞M*) ≤ ∫⁻_{B_p} θ d((H^n⌞M)⌞M*), and ((H^n⌞M)⌞M*)(B_p) = H^n(B_p ∩ M*) ≤ H^n(F ∩ M*) ≤ H^n(N_0) = 0, so this integral is 0. Hence μ_V(F_p) = 0 for every p and μ_V(F) = 0 (F ⊆ U = ⋃_p K_p); moreover μ_V(U^c) = V(U^c × G) = 0 (Varifold.supported, Varifold.weight_apply). So μ_V-a.e. x lies in U ∖ F, i.e. HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ(x)) with θ(x) = m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, and ofReal θ(x) = (m : ℝ≥0∞). Taking k := m gives ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ HasDensity n μ_V x k for μ_V-a.e. x. ∎

Hence Θ^n(μ_V,x) = θ(x) ∈ ℕ_{≥1} at every x ∈ M* off an H^n-null set N_0.

subproblem.title: Homothetic rescalings restricted to open sets preserve integrality
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U, O ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U and W an n-varifold on O (so U and O are open), ξ ∈ ℝ^N and t > 0 with ξ + t·y ∈ U for every y ∈ O. If V is integral and W.measure = (rescaledMeasure V ξ t).restrict (O × G(N,n)), i.e. W = V_{ξ,t} ⌞ G_n(O), then W is integral.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U O : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (W : Varifold N n O) (ξ : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → (∀ y ∈ O, ξ + t • y ∈ U) → IsIntegral V → W.measure = (rescaledMeasure V ξ t).restrict (O ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → IsIntegral W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step B4 of the parent proof of Simon 8.5.9 ("each W_k is integral: homotheties and restriction to open sets preserve IsVarifoldOf with integer θ; approximate tangent planes are local and homothety-invariant; H^n(ξ + λA) = λ^n H^n(A)"), written out. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; H^n := μHE[n]; approx(M,θ,x,S) abbreviates HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane; rescaledMeasure V ξ t = ofReal(t^{-n}) • (V.measure).map Φ with Φ(z,S) := (t^{-1}(z − ξ), S).

1. The similarity. Let σ(y) := ξ + t y and η := σ^{-1}, η(x) = t^{-1}(x − ξ); both are homeomorphisms, hence measurable equivalences, of ℝ^N. For every A ⊆ ℝ^N, H^n(σ(A)) = t^n H^n(A) and H^n(η(A)) = t^{-n} H^n(A) (translation invariance of μHE[n] together with Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ / MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Consequently σ and η map H^n-null sets to H^n-null sets, Borel sets to Borel sets and H^n-null-measurable sets to H^n-null-measurable sets. Moreover, for every A ⊆ ℝ^N (measurable or not), H^n⌞σ(A) = t^n·σ_#(H^n⌞A) as measures: for Borel B, σ_#(H^n⌞A)(B) = H^n(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A) = H^n(η(B ∩ σ(A))) = t^{-n}H^n(B ∩ σ(A)). Hence, by MeasureTheory.lintegral_map_equiv (for the measurable equivalence σ), ∫⁻_{σ(A)} g dH^n = t^n ∫⁻_A g∘σ dH^n for every g : ℝ^N → [0,∞] and every A ⊆ ℝ^N; likewise ∫⁻_{η(A)} g dH^n = t^{-n} ∫⁻_A g∘η dH^n.

2. Data. By IsIntegral V choose M, θ with IsVarifoldOf V M θ and θ ∈ ℕ for (H^n⌞M)-a.e. point. Define M̂ := {y ∈ O : σ(y) ∈ M} = O ∩ η(M) and θ̂ := θ∘σ. We verify IsVarifoldOf W M̂ θ̂ (steps 3–9) and integrality (step 10).

3. M̂ ⊆ O by definition.

4. M̂ is H^n-null-measurable, because η(M) is (step 1; M is H^n-null-measurable) and O is open.

5. M̂ is countably n-rectifiable. CountablyRectifiable n M gives M_0 with H^n(M_0) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Then η(M) ⊆ η(M_0) ∪ ⋃_j (η∘F_j)(ℝ^n), H^n(η(M_0)) = t^{-n}H^n(M_0) = 0, and η∘F_j is Lipschitz (constant Lip(F_j)/t). So η(M) is countably n-rectifiable, and so is its subset M̂ (CountablyRectifiable.mono).

6. θ̂(y) = θ(σ(y)) > 0 for y ∈ M̂, since σ(y) ∈ M.

7. Local integrability. Let K ⊆ O be compact. Then σ(K) is compact and σ(K) ⊆ U by the hypothesis ξ + t y ∈ U (y ∈ O), so θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ σ(K). Since K ⊆ O, M̂ ∩ K = η(M ∩ σ(K)), and by step 1 (with g := |θ|∘σ, so g∘η = |θ|), ∫⁻_{M̂∩K} |θ̂| dH^n = ∫⁻_{η(M∩σ(K))} |θ|∘σ dH^n = t^{-n} ∫⁻_{M∩σ(K)} |θ| dH^n < ∞. A Borel function θ_K with θ_K = θ H^n-a.e. on M ∩ σ(K) gives the Borel function θ_K∘σ, equal to θ̂ H^n-a.e. on M̂ ∩ K (η maps null sets to null sets); so θ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable on M̂ ∩ K, hence H^n-integrable there.

8. Approximate tangent planes are local and homothety-invariant. Claim: for y ∈ O and S ∈ G, approx(M̂, θ̂, y, S) ⇔ approx(M, θ, σ(y), S). Put x := σ(y). For r > 0: blowUpMap y r '' M̂ = {r^{-1}(w − y) : w ∈ O, σ(w) ∈ M}, while blowUpMap x (tr) '' M = {(tr)^{-1}(z − x) : z ∈ M} = {r^{-1}(w − y) : σ(w) ∈ M} (substitute z = σ(w) and use (tr)^{-1}(σ(w) − σ(y)) = r^{-1}(w − y)). Moreover θ̂(y + r v) = θ(x + (tr)v) and θ̂(y) = θ(x). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with support in B_R(0) (closed ball). If O = ℝ^N, or rR < dist(y, ℝ^N ∖ O), then y + r v ∈ O for every |v| ≤ R, so the two (possibly non-measurable) image sets have the same intersection with B_R(0). Since f vanishes off B_R(0), each set integral equals the integral of the same function against H^n restricted to (image set) ∩ B_R(0) (Measure.restrict_restrict for the Borel set B_R(0)); these restricted measures coincide, so integrability and the values agree: ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M̂} f(v) θ̂(y + r v) dH^n(v) = ∫_{blowUpMap x (tr) '' M} f(v) θ(x + (tr)v) dH^n(v). Since r ↦ tr maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0 (t > 0) and the prescribed limits θ̂(y)∫_{S.plane} f dH^n and θ(x)∫_{S.plane} f dH^n are equal, the left side converges to its prescribed limit iff the right side does; the condition finrank S.plane = n is common to both definitions. This proves the claim.

9. Representation identity. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N × G be Borel. By Measure.restrict_apply, Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (Φ is measurable, A ∩ (O × G) is Borel): W(A) = (rescaledMeasure V ξ t)(A ∩ (O × G)) = t^{-n} V(Φ^{-1}(A ∩ (O × G))). Φ^{-1}(A ∩ (O×G)) is Borel, so by IsVarifoldOf V M θ: V(Φ^{-1}(A ∩ (O × G))) = ∫⁻_{E_1} θ dH^n with E_1 := {x ∈ M : ∃ S, approx(M,θ,x,S) ∧ η(x) ∈ O ∧ (η(x), S) ∈ A}. Now E_1 = σ(E_2) with E_2 := {y ∈ O : σ(y) ∈ M ∧ ∃ S, approx(M, θ, σ(y), S) ∧ (y,S) ∈ A}, and by step 8, E_2 = {y ∈ M̂ : ∃ S, approx(M̂, θ̂, y, S) ∧ (y,S) ∈ A}. By step 1: W(A) = t^{-n}∫⁻_{σ(E_2)} ofReal θ dH^n = t^{-n} t^n ∫⁻_{E_2} ofReal(θ∘σ) dH^n = ∫⁻_{E_2} ofReal θ̂ dH^n. Together with steps 3–7 this proves IsVarifoldOf W M̂ θ̂.

10. Integer multiplicity. Y := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ∉ ℕ} is H^n-null (M is H^n-null-measurable and θ ∈ ℕ (H^n⌞M)-a.e., ae_restrict_iff'₀). {y ∈ M̂ : θ̂(y) ∉ ℕ} ⊆ η(Y), which is H^n-null by step 1. Since M̂ is H^n-null-measurable, ∃ k ∈ ℕ, θ̂(y) = k holds for (H^n⌞M̂)-a.e. y. With step 9, IsIntegral W holds with witnesses M̂, θ̂. ∎
proof_key_steps: The similarity σ(y) = ξ + ty scales H^n by t^n on all sets, so it preserves null sets, Borel and null-measurable sets, and ∫_{σ(A)} g dH^n = t^n ∫_A g∘σ dH^n.
Carrier M̂ := O ∩ σ^{-1}(M), multiplicity θ̂ := θ∘σ: null-measurable, countably n-rectifiable (η∘F_j Lipschitz), positive, locally integrable (σ(K) ⊆ U compact).
Weighted approximate tangent planes are local and homothety invariant: approx(M̂,θ̂,y,S) ⇔ approx(M,θ,σ(y),S) for y ∈ O.
Change of variables gives the IsVarifoldOf identity for W; θ̂ ∈ ℕ H^n-a.e. on M̂ since η maps null sets to null sets.

subproblem.title: Besicovitch bound liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(x)) ≤ c(x)ρ^n almost everywhere (step B3, printed (1)–(2))
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ν_i (i ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^N with sup_i ν_i(W) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (IsRelCompactOpenIn W U). Suppose that for μ-a.e. x the density Θ^n(μ,x) exists and is finite. Then for μ-a.e. x there are c ∈ ℝ and r > 0 such that liminf_{i→∞} ν_i(B_ρ(x)) ≤ cρ^n (as ENNReal.ofReal(cρ^n)) for every ρ ∈ (0, r).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (ν : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N)), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ W : Set (Euclidean N), IsRelCompactOpenIn W U → ⨆ i, ν i W ≠ ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, HasDensity n μ x θ ∧ θ ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ c r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r → liminf (fun i ↦ ν i (closedBall x ρ)) atTop ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the printed estimates (1)–(2) in the proof of Simon 8.5.9 (step B3 of the parent proof), stated for general measures; in the application μ = μ_V (the limit varifold's weight) and ν_i = ‖δV_{φ(i)}‖. Notation: B_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞); W ⊂⊂ U means IsRelCompactOpenIn W U; all quantities are in [0,∞]; HasDensity n μ x θ means μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0.

1. Localisation. Fix an open W ⊂⊂ U. If W = ∅ put A_W := ∅ below (nothing to prove). Otherwise, since closure W is compact and U is open, choose r_W ∈ (0,1] with cthickening r_W (closure W) ⊆ U (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and let W̃ := thickening r_W W = {y : infDist y W < r_W}. W̃ is open and bounded, and closure W̃ ⊆ cthickening r_W (closure W), a compact subset of U (closed and bounded); so W̃ ⊂⊂ U and S_W := sup_i ν_i(W̃) < ∞ by hypothesis. For ξ ∈ W and 0 < ρ < r_W, B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ W̃ (every point of B_ρ(ξ) has distance ≤ ρ < r_W from ξ ∈ W).

2. Relative bound on W. Let A_W := {ξ ∈ W : there is no c ∈ ℝ with liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(c)·μ(B_ρ(ξ)) for all ρ ∈ (0, r_W)}. Claim: μ(A_W) = 0 (outer measure). Fix an integer j ≥ 1. For ξ ∈ A_W the constant c = j fails, so there is ρ_ξ ∈ (0, r_W) with liminf_i ν_i(B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ)) > j·μ(B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ)); since a liminf strictly exceeds a value only if the sequence eventually exceeds it (Mathlib Filter.eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf; [0,∞] is a complete lattice), there is i_ξ ∈ ℕ with ν_i(B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ)) > j·μ(B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ)) for all i ≥ i_ξ. For i ∈ ℕ let A_{W,i} := {ξ ∈ A_W : i_ξ ≤ i}; these sets increase with i and their union is A_W. Fix i. Apply the Besicovitch covering theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.12; SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_besicovitchCovering_families, from Mathlib Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families) to the closed balls B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ), ξ ∈ A_{W,i} (radii in (0,1]): there are N_B = N_B(N) subfamilies 𝓑_1, …, 𝓑_{N_B}, each consisting of pairwise disjoint balls, whose union covers A_{W,i}. Each 𝓑_l is countable (pairwise disjoint sets with non-empty interior in the separable space ℝ^N: Mathlib Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior). Every B ∈ 𝓑_l is some B_{ρ_ξ}(ξ) with ξ ∈ A_{W,i}, so i ≥ i_ξ and μ(B) < j^{-1}ν_i(B); and B ⊆ W̃. Therefore μ(A_{W,i}) ≤ Σ_l Σ_{B∈𝓑_l} μ(B) ≤ j^{-1} Σ_l Σ_{B∈𝓑_l} ν_i(B) = j^{-1} Σ_l ν_i(⋃𝓑_l) ≤ j^{-1} N_B ν_i(W̃) ≤ N_B S_W / j. By continuity of the outer measure along increasing sequences of arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) sets (Mathlib Monotone.measure_iUnion), μ(A_W) = sup_i μ(A_{W,i}) ≤ N_B S_W / j. As j is arbitrary and S_W < ∞, μ(A_W) = 0.

3. Exhaustion. If U = ∅ then μ = 0 (μ(U^c) = 0) and the claim is trivial. Otherwise let K_p (p ∈ ℕ) be compact with K_p ⊆ interior K_{p+1} and ⋃_p K_p = U, and W_p := interior K_p: W_p is open, closure W_p ⊆ K_p is compact and contained in U, so W_p ⊂⊂ U, and ⋃_p W_p = U. By step 2 the set A := (ℝ^N ∖ U) ∪ ⋃_p A_{W_p} is μ-null (μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 by hypothesis; the hypothesis μ(K) < ∞ is not needed). Every ξ ∉ A lies in some W_p and, since ξ ∉ A_{W_p}, there is c_1 ∈ ℝ with liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(c_1)·μ(B_ρ(ξ)) for all ρ ∈ (0, r_{W_p}); replacing c_1 by max{c_1, 0} we may assume c_1 ≥ 0.

4. From μ(B_ρ(ξ)) to ρ^n. Let D be the μ-null set of points ξ at which Θ^n(μ, ξ) does not exist as a finite value. For ξ ∉ A ∪ D let θ_ξ := Θ^n(μ, ξ) ∈ [0,∞) and p, c_1 as in step 3. Since μ(B_ρ(ξ))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ_ξ < θ_ξ + 1, there is r' > 0 with μ(B_ρ(ξ)) ≤ ofReal((θ_ξ + 1)ω_nρ^n) for 0 < ρ < r' (using the real values of θ_ξ and of ω_n ∈ (0,∞)). subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, and V_i (i ∈ ℕ), V n-varifolds on U (U open) such that V_i → V as Radon measures on G_n(U) (RadonConverges), every V_i is integral with locally bounded first variation, V has tangent plane P ∈ G(N,n) with multiplicity θ₀ at ξ (HasTangentPlane V ξ P θ₀; so ξ ∈ U, θ₀ > 0), and for some c ∈ ℝ, r > 0: liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(B_ρ(ξ)) ≤ cρ^n for every ρ ∈ (0,r). Then there are n-varifolds W_k (k ∈ ℕ) on the open ball B°_5(0), each integral with locally bounded first variation, such that ‖δW_k‖(B°_5(0)) → 0 and ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G(N,n).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the printed steps (3)–(4) in the proof of Simon 8.5.9 (step B4 of the parent proof), with the blow-ups restricted to the fixed ball B°_5(0) instead of B°_k(0); integrality of each blow-up is the sibling rescaled_integral. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact); μ_V := V.weight; ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V; B_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ, B°_ρ(x) := ball x ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞); v(P) := planeVarifoldMeasure P; V'_{ξ,λ} := rescaledMeasure V' ξ λ; O := B°_5(0).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Transfer of the convergence. If F ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) and tsupport F ⊆ U × G, then ∫ F dV_i → ∫ F dV. Indeed the restriction of F to the open subspace U ×ˢ univ is continuous with compact support (tsupport F is a compact subset of U × G), so RadonConverges applies to it, and ∫ F|_{U×G} d(V_i.domainMeasure) = ∫ F dV_i.measure because domainMeasure is the comap of V_i.measure along the inclusion of the measurable set U × G and V_i.measure vanishes off U × G (likewise for V).
 (b) Rescaled integrals. For every varifold V' on U, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) and λ > 0: ∫ f dV'_{ξ,λ} = λ^{-n} ∫ f(λ^{-1}(z − ξ), S) dV'(z,S) (definition of rescaledMeasure, integral_map, integral_smul_measure).
 (c) Let c' := max{c, 1}. For 0 < ρ < r: liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(B_ρ(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(cρ^n) ≤ ofReal(c'ρ^n) < ofReal(2c'ρ^n).
 (d) Mass of V near ξ. HasTangentPlane V ξ P θ₀ gives ξ ∈ U, θ₀ > 0 and ∫ f dV_{ξ,λ} → θ₀∫ f dv(P) as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G). Let χ_7 : ℝ → [0,1] be continuous with χ_7 = 1 on (−∞,6] and χ_7 = 0 on [7,∞); (z,S) ↦ χ_7(|z|) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G). Hence λ^{-n}∫ χ_7(|z − ξ|/λ) dμ_V(z) → θ₀∫_{P.plane} χ_7(|y|) dH^n(y) ≤ θ₀H^n(P.plane ∩ B_7(0)) = θ₀ω_n7^n (H^n(P.plane ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n s^n: P.plane is isometric to ℝ^n, on which μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure; Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). As 1_{B_{6λ}(ξ)}(z) ≤ χ_7(|z − ξ|/λ), there is λ̄ > 0 with μ_V(B_{6λ}(ξ)) ≤ (θ₀ω_n7^n + 1)λ^n for 0 < λ < λ̄.

1. A countable dense family. Let 𝓕 := {f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) : tsupport f ⊆ O × G}. There are f_m ∈ 𝓕 (m ∈ ℕ) such that every f ∈ 𝓕 is a uniform limit of functions from {f_m}. For instance: for each integer R ≥ 1 fix a continuous ψ_R : ℝ^N → [0,1] equal to 1 on B_{5−1/R}(0) and to 0 outside B°_{5−1/(2R)}(0), and take all products ψ_R(z)·π(z,S) with π a polynomial with rational coefficients in the coordinates of z and the matrix entries of S. This family is countable and contained in 𝓕. If f ∈ 𝓕, then tsupport f ⊆ B_{5−1/R}(0) × G for some R (compactness); by Stone–Weierstrass on the compact set B_{5−1/(2R)}(0) × G (polynomials in the coordinates of z and the entries of S.1 form a point-separating subalgebra containing constants) there are real polynomials converging uniformly to f there, and replacing their coefficients by nearby rationals keeps uniform convergence on this compact set; so there are rational polynomials π_l → f uniformly on B_{5−1/(2R)}(0) × G, whence ψ_R π_l → ψ_R f = f uniformly on ℝ^N × G (both sides vanish off B°_{5−1/(2R)}(0) × G).

2. Choice of scales. For each integer k ≥ 1 choose λ_k > 0 with (i) λ_k ≤ 1/k; (ii) 6λ_k < r and B_{7λ_k}(ξ) ⊆ U (U is open and ξ ∈ U); (iii) λ_k < λ̄; (iv) |∫ f_m dV_{ξ,λ_k} − θ₀∫ f_m dv(P)| < 1/k for all m ≤ k (finitely many conditions, each valid for all small λ by HasTangentPlane V ξ P θ₀).

3. Choice of indices. Put i_0 := 0. For k ≥ 1 choose i_k > i_{k−1} such that (v) ‖δV_{i_k}‖(B_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ ofReal(2c'(5λ_k)^n); (vi) |∫ f_m d(V_{i_k})_{ξ,λ_k} − ∫ f_m dV_{ξ,λ_k}| < 1/k for all m ≤ k; (vii) μ_{V_{i_k}}(B_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ (θ₀ω_n7^n + 2)λ_k^n. This is possible: (v) holds for infinitely many i by 0(c), as 5λ_k < r and a liminf strictly below a value is frequently below it; (vi) holds for all large i, because by 0(b) ∫ f_m dV'_{ξ,λ_k} = λ_k^{-n}∫ F_{m,k} dV' with F_{m,k}(z,S) := f_m(λ_k^{-1}(z − ξ), S) ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G), tsupport F_{m,k} ⊆ B°_{5λ_k}(ξ) × G ⊆ U × G, and 0(a) applies; (vii) holds for all large i: with χ' : ℝ → [0,1] continuous, χ' = 1 on (−∞,5], χ' = 0 on [6,∞), and F_k(z,S) := χ'(|z − ξ|/λ_k) ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G), tsupport F_k ⊆ B_{6λ_k}(ξ) × G ⊆ U × G, we have μ_{V_i}(B_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ ∫ F_k dV_i → ∫ F_k dV ≤ μ_V(B_{6λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ (θ₀ω_n7^n + 1)λ_k^n by 0(a), 0(d) and (iii).

4. The varifolds. For k ≥ 1 let m_k := ((V_{i_k})_{ξ,λ_k}).restrict (O × G). This is the measure of an n-varifold W_k on O: O is open; m_k((ℝ^N ∖ O) × G) = 0; and for compact K ⊆ O, m_k(K × G) ≤ λ_k^{-n} V_{i_k}(σ_k(K) × G) < ∞, where σ_k(y) := ξ + λ_k y, because the preimage of K × G under (z,S) ↦ (λ_k^{-1}(z − ξ), S) is σ_k(K) × G and σ_k(K) is a compact subset of B°_{5λ_k}(ξ) ⊆ U (finite_on_compact of V_{i_k}). Put W_0 := W_1.

5. Integrality. For y ∈ O, ξ + λ_k y ∈ B°_{5λ_k}(ξ) ⊆ U. The sibling rescaled_integral, applied to U, O, V := V_{i_k} (integral), W := W_k, ξ and t := λ_k > 0 (W_k.measure = (rescaledMeasure V_{i_k} ξ λ_k).restrict (O × G) by construction), shows that W_k is integral.

6. First-variation scaling (printed (4)). Let X be a test field on O (Varifold.TestVectorField O) and Y(z) := λ_k X(λ_k^{-1}(z − ξ)). Y is C¹ with tsupport Y = σ_k(tsupport X), a compact subset of B°_{5λ_k}(ξ) ⊆ U, so Y is a test field on U; DY(z) = DX(λ_k^{-1}(z − ξ)), hence div_S Y(z) = (div_S X)(λ_k^{-1}(z − ξ)) for every S ∈ G (tangentialDivergence only involves the derivative). By 0(b), and because div_S X vanishes off tsupport X ⊆ O (so the restriction to O × G is immaterial): δW_k(X) = ∫ div_S X dm_k = λ_k^{-n} ∫ div_S Y(z) dV_{i_k}(z,S) = λ_k^{-n} δV_{i_k}(Y). Since V_{i_k} has locally bounded first variation, ‖δV_{i_k}‖ = variationMeasure V_{i_k} = firstVariationRieszMeasure, and the polar representation (SimonGMT Varifold.isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz: δV_{i_k}(Y) = −∫⟨ν, Y⟩ d‖δV_{i_k}‖ with |ν| = 1 ‖δV_{i_k}‖-a.e.) gives |δV_{i_k}(Y)| ≤ ∫ |Y| d‖δV_{i_k}‖ ≤ λ_k (sup|X|) ‖δV_{i_k}‖(B_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ λ_k (sup|X|) 2c'5^nλ_k^n by (v). Hence |δW_k(X)| ≤ 2c'5^n λ_k sup|X| for every test field X on O, wherever its support lies in O (this uniformity is what controls ‖δW_k‖ on the whole domain O).

 (b) For j ≥ 1, O_j := B°_{5−1/j}(0) is open with compact closure in O, so ‖δW_k‖(O_j) = firstVariationNormOn W_k O_j ≤ 2c'5^nλ_k (SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm); as O_j ↑ O, ‖δW_k‖(O) = sup_j ‖δW_k‖(O_j) ≤ 2c'5^nλ_k ≤ 2c'5^n/k. Hence ‖δW_k‖(B°_5(0)) → 0.

7. Convergence (printed (3)). For m ≤ k, since f_m vanishes off O × G, ∫ f_m dW_k = ∫ f_m d(V_{i_k})_{ξ,λ_k}, so by (iv) and (vi) |∫ f_m dW_k − θ₀∫ f_m dv(P)| < 2/k; hence ∫ f_m dW_k → θ₀∫ f_m dv(P) for every m. Uniform mass bound: μ_{W_k}(O) = m_k(O × G) = λ_k^{-n}μ_{V_{i_k}}(B°_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ θ₀ω_n7^n + 2 =: C_M by (vii), and θ₀·v(P)(O × G) = θ₀H^n(P.plane ∩ O) ≤ θ₀ω_n5^n ≤ C_M. Let f ∈ 𝓕 and η > 0, and choose m with sup|f − f_m| < η (step 1). As f − f_m vanishes off O × G, |∫(f − f_m) dW_k| ≤ ηC_M and θ₀|∫(f − f_m) dv(P)| ≤ ηC_M, so limsup_k |∫ f dW_k − θ₀∫ f dv(P)| ≤ 2ηC_M. As η > 0 is arbitrary, ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P).

Steps 4–7 give n-varifolds W_k on B°_5(0) that are integral, have locally bounded first variation, satisfy ‖δW_k‖(B°_5(0)) → 0, and satisfy ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G. ∎

Choose λ_k ↓ 0 (blow-up accuracy for f_m, m ≤ k) and then i_k ↑ with ‖δV_{i_k}‖(B_{5λ_k}(ξ)) ≤ 2c'(5λ_k)^n, closeness of rescaled integrals and mass bounds.

subproblem.title: Integral varifolds with vanishing first variation converging to θ₀ v(P) force θ₀ ∈ ℕ (step B6, repaired conclusion of 5.9)
subproblem.statement: Assume AllardRectifiabilityTheorem, FirstRectifiabilityTheorem, MonotonicityFormula (frozen contract statements) and the tangent-graph-cover statement: for 0 < L ≤ 1, every varifold V on any U and every P ∈ G(N,n) there are closed sets Γ_i, each an L-Lipschitz graph over P, containing every point at which V has a tangent plane T with |p_T v − p_P v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v. Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n), θ₀ > 0, and W_k (k ∈ ℕ) n-varifolds on the open ball B°_5(0) such that each W_k is integral with locally bounded first variation, ‖δW_k‖(B°_5(0)) → 0, and ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G(N,n). Then θ₀ is a natural number.
subproblem.lean_statement: AllardRectifiabilityTheorem → FirstRectifiabilityTheorem → MonotonicityFormula → (∀ (N n : ℕ) (L : ℝ), 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → ∀ (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n), ∃ Γ : ℕ → Set (Euclidean N), (∀ i, IsClosed (Γ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ y ∈ Γ i, ∀ z ∈ Γ i, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) ∧ ∀ (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → (∀ v : Euclidean N, ‖Grassmannian.project T v - Grassmannian.project P v‖ ≤ L / 4 * ‖v‖) → ∃ i, x ∈ Γ i) → ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (θ₀ : ℝ) (W : ℕ → Varifold N n (ball (0 : Euclidean N) 5)), 0 < θ₀ → (∀ k, IsIntegral (W k)) → (∀ k, (W k).HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation) → Tendsto (fun k ↦ variationMeasure (W k) (ball (0 : Euclidean N) 5)) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ f : C_c(Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n, ℝ), tsupport f ⊆ ball (0 : Euclidean N) 5 ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)) → Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫ z, f z ∂(W k).measure) atTop (𝓝 (θ₀ * ∫ z, f z ∂(planeVarifoldMeasure P)))) → ∃ m : ℕ, θ₀ = m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 8.5.9, the printed proof "that V is integer multiplicity if the V_i are" (pp. 218–219), with the repaired conclusion of step B6 of the parent proof. ERRATUM (E3): the printed conclusion from (7) ∫fψ_i → θ0∫f and (8) ψ_i ≤ θ0 + ε_i off A_i with L^n(A_i) → 0 is incomplete (mass of ψ_i may concentrate over A_i), and "max{ψ_i, N}" must read "min{ψ_i, N}". Instead, the good part of every fibre sum is bounded by an integer k₀, the bad part is controlled by its mass ≤ c₀ε, and mass is compared with fibre sums through Lipschitz graphs of small slope (no area formula on rectifiable carriers). Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact); O := B°_5(0) = ball 0 5; μ_k := μ_{W_k} = (W_k).weight; ‖δW‖ := variationMeasure W; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞), also used for its real value; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T; W_{y,ρ} := rescaledMeasure W y ρ; p := Grassmannian.project P, q := id − p; t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖, the operator norm of p_S − p; t_P(P) = 0, |(p_S − p)v| ≤ t_P(S)|v|, and S ↦ t_P(S) is continuous (S ↦ S.1 is continuous, S.1 ↦ projectionLinearMap S is the linear map (LinearMap.toMatrix b b).symm between finite-dimensional spaces, LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap is a linear equivalence between finite-dimensional spaces, and the norm is continuous); as G is compact (Grassmannian.instCompactSpace / closed and bounded set of matrices), (z,S) ↦ χ(|z|)t_P(S) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G) for every continuous compactly supported χ. (H) denotes the convergence hypothesis ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P) for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ O × G.

0. Consequences of (H). (a) If K is compact, O' is open, K ⊆ O' and the closure of O' is a compact subset of O, then limsup_k μ_k(K) ≤ θ₀H^n(P.plane ∩ O'): choose a continuous g : ℝ^N → [0,1] with g = 1 on K and compact support in O' (Urysohn); f(z,S) := g(z) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ O × G, so μ_k(K) ≤ ∫ g dμ_k = ∫ f dW_k → θ₀∫ f dv(P) = θ₀∫_{P.plane} g dH^n ≤ θ₀H^n(P.plane ∩ O'). (b) For every continuous g ≥ 0 with compact support in O, ∫ g dμ_k → θ₀∫_{P.plane} g dH^n (apply (H) to f(z,S) := g(z)). (c) For an n-plane T, a ∈ T.plane and s > 0: H^n(T.plane ∩ B_s(a)) = H^n(T.plane ∩ B°_s(a)) = ω_n s^n (T.plane is isometric to ℝ^n, on which μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

1. Case n = 0. A symmetric idempotent real matrix with trace 0 is 0 (Σ_{ij}P_ij² = trace(PᵀP) = trace(P) = 0), so G(N,0) = {0}, P = 0 and P.plane = {0}. μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib), and μH[0]{x} = 1 (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), so by countable additivity μH[0] restricted to a countable set S is Σ_{x∈S} δ_x; in particular θ₀v(P) is θ₀ times the unit point mass at (0,P). Fix k. By IsIntegral W_k choose M_k, θ_k with IsVarifoldOf W_k M_k θ_k and θ_k ∈ ℕ (H^0⌞M_k)-a.e. Countable 0-rectifiability gives M_k ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^0) with H^0(M_0) = 0, so M_0 = ∅ and M_k is countable; points have H^0-measure 1, so θ_k(x) ∈ ℕ, hence θ_k(x) ∈ {1,2,…}, for every x ∈ M_k. For Borel B, μ_k(B) = W_k(B × G) = ∫⁻_{M_k^* ∩ B} θ_k dH^0 = Σ_{x ∈ M_k^* ∩ B} θ_k(x) ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞} (M_k^* ⊆ M_k the approximate tangent points; a lintegral over a countable set against the counting measure is the sum). Choose continuous g_1, g_2 with 1_{B_{1/4}(0)} ≤ g_1 ≤ 1_{B_{1/2}(0)} ≤ g_2 ≤ 1_{B_{3/4}(0)}. By 0(b), ∫ g_i dμ_k → θ₀g_i(0) = θ₀, and ∫ g_1 dμ_k ≤ μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) ≤ ∫ g_2 dμ_k, so μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → θ₀ ∈ (0,∞). A sequence in ℕ ∪ {∞} converging to a real number is eventually a natural number within distance 1/3 of it, hence eventually constant, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ.

2. Case n ≥ 1: set-up. Put Λ := θ₀ω_n3^n + 1 ≥ 1 and apply the sibling allard_lemma (with the hypothesis MonotonicityFormula, N, n, Λ; 1 ≤ n, 1 ≤ Λ): this gives δ̄ > 0 and c₀ ≥ 0. Suppose, for a contradiction, that θ₀ ∉ ℕ, and let k₀ := ⌊θ₀⌋ ∈ ℕ, so k₀ < θ₀ < k₀ + 1. Fix a continuous ψ : ℝ → [0,1] with ψ = 1 on (−∞,1/4] and ψ = 0 on [1/2,∞), and let I₀ := ∫_{P.plane} ψ(|a|) dH^n(a); by 0(c), ω_n4^{-n} ≤ I₀ ≤ ω_n2^{-n}, so 0 < I₀ < ∞.

3. Claim. Let δ ∈ (0,δ̄] satisfy (1+δ)(θ₀+δ) + δ < k₀ + 1 and 4δ⁴ ≤ ω_n, and put ε := δ⁴ and L := 4ε/ω_n ∈ (0,1]. Then θ₀I₀ ≤ c₀ε + (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀I₀. Steps 4–11 prove this claim.

4. Choice of k. For all sufficiently large k:
 (i) μ_k(B°_3(0)) ≤ Λ: by 0(a),(c) with K := B_3(0) and O' := B°_{3+η}(0) (η ∈ (0,1) with θ₀ω_n(3+η)^n < Λ), limsup_k μ_k(B_3(0)) ≤ θ₀ω_n(3+η)^n < Λ.
 (ii) ‖δW_k‖(B°_3(0)) ≤ ‖δW_k‖(O) < ε², by the hypothesis ‖δW_k‖(O) → 0.
 (iii) ∫⁻_{B°_3(0)×G} t_P dW_k < ε²: let χ : ℝ → [0,1] be continuous with χ = 1 on (−∞,3] and χ = 0 on [4,∞); (z,S) ↦ χ(|z|)t_P(S) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport in B_4(0) × G ⊆ O × G, so ∫⁻_{B°_3(0)×G} t_P dW_k ≤ ∫ χ(|z|)t_P(S) dW_k → θ₀∫ χ(|z|)t_P(S) dv(P) = θ₀∫_{P.plane} χ(|z|)t_P(P) dH^n = 0.
 (iv) μ_k(B_1(a)) ≤ (θ₀ + δ)ω_n for every a ∈ P.plane with |a| ≤ 1: choose η ∈ (0,1) with θ₀(1+2η)^n ≤ θ₀ + δ/2 and finitely many a_l ∈ P.plane, |a_l| ≤ 1, with {a ∈ P.plane : |a| ≤ 1} ⊆ ⋃_l B°_η(a_l) (compactness). By 0(a),(c) with K := B_{1+η}(a_l) and O' := B°_{1+2η}(a_l) (its closure lies in B_4(0) ⊆ O), limsup_k μ_k(B_{1+η}(a_l)) ≤ θ₀ω_n(1+2η)^n ≤ (θ₀ + δ/2)ω_n < (θ₀ + δ)ω_n; and each B_1(a) with a ∈ P.plane, |a| ≤ 1, lies in some B_{1+η}(a_l).
 Fix such a k and write W := W_k, μ := μ_k.

5. The bad set. W is an n-varifold on O ⊇ B°_3(0) with locally bounded first variation which, by 4(i)–(iii), satisfies μ(B°_3(0)) ≤ Λ, ‖δW‖(B°_3(0)) < ε² and ∫⁻_{B°_3(0)×G} t_P dW < ε²; and δ ∈ (0,δ̄], ε ∈ (0,δ⁴]. By the sibling allard_lemma: (a) the set E of y ∈ B_2(0) ∩ spt μ that violate (1) ‖δW‖(B_ρ(y)) ≤ εμ(B_ρ(y)) ∀ρ ∈ (0,1) or (2) ∫_{B_ρ(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ερ^n ∀ρ ∈ (0,1) has μ(E) ≤ c₀ε; (b) the fibre bound holds. Let E' := toMeasurable μ E, a Borel set with E ⊆ E' and μ(E') = μ(E) ≤ c₀ε.

6. Canonical form of W. By the sibling integral_density, for μ-a.e. y there is m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, with HasDensity n μ y m; in particular Θ^n(μ,y) exists and is > 0 μ-a.e. By the sibling canonical_representation (with the hypotheses AllardRectifiabilityTheorem and FirstRectifiabilityTheorem; W has locally bounded first variation) there is θ̃ : ℝ^N → ℝ with IsVarifoldOf W M̃ θ̃, where M̃ := {y ∈ spt μ : ∃ T θ', HasTangentPlane W y T θ'}, such that every y ∈ M̃ has some T(y) ∈ G with HasTangentPlane W y T(y) θ̃(y) and HasDensity n μ y (ofReal θ̃(y)), and every μ-null Z ⊆ M̃ is H^n-null. Let Z := {y ∈ M̃ : there is no m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1 and θ̃(y) = m}. If y ∈ Z had HasDensity n μ y m with m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, then by uniqueness of limits (𝓝[>]0 is non-trivial and [0,∞] is Hausdorff) ofReal θ̃(y) = m, and θ̃(y) > 0 (IsVarifoldOf) gives θ̃(y) = m, which is impossible. So Z lies in the μ-null exceptional set of integral_density, μ(Z) = 0, and therefore H^n(Z) = 0. Moreover, for Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N, IsVarifoldOf with A := (B ∩ B_2(0)) × G gives μ(B ∩ B_2(0)) = ∫⁻_{M̃^* ∩ B ∩ B_2(0)} θ̃ dH^n ≤ ∫⁻_{M̃ ∩ B_2(0) ∩ B} θ̃ dH^n (M̃^* ⊆ M̃ the approximate tangent points; Measure.restrict_mono). By IsVarifoldOf, θ̃ is H^n-integrable on M̃ ∩ B_2(0) (B_2(0) is a compact subset of O), so ofReal∘θ̃ is a.e.-measurable for H^n⌞(M̃ ∩ B_2(0)); hence μ⌞B_2(0) ≤ (H^n⌞(M̃ ∩ B_2(0))).withDensity(ofReal θ̃) as measures, and by lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀, ∫⁻ u dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M̃ ∩ B_2(0)} u θ̃ dH^n for every Borel u ≥ 0 vanishing off B_2(0).

7. Good flat points. Let G' := {y ∈ M̃ ∖ E' : |p(y)| < 1, |q(y)| < ε, θ̃(y) ∈ {1,2,…}} = ((M̃ ∖ Z) ∖ E') ∩ {|p| < 1} ∩ {|q| < ε}; G' is H^n-null-measurable (M̃ is H^n-null-measurable by IsVarifoldOf, Z is H^n-null, E' is Borel, the last two sets are open). Let y ∈ G'. Then |y|² = |p(y)|² + |q(y)|² < 1 + ε² < 4, so y ∈ B_2(0); y ∈ spt μ (M̃ ⊆ spt μ); and y ∉ E ⊆ E'. Hence y satisfies (1) and (2). Let T := T(y) and θ_y := θ̃(y) ≥ 1. For κ ∈ (0,1) let χ_κ : ℝ → [0,1] be continuous with χ_κ = 1 on (−∞,κ] and χ_κ = 0 on [1,∞), and f_κ(z,S) := χ_κ(|z|)t_P(S) ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G). For ρ ∈ (0,1), by the formula for rescaled integrals and (2): ∫ f_κ dW_{y,ρ} = ρ^{-n}∫ χ_κ(|z − y|/ρ) t_P(S) dW(z,S) ≤ ρ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ(y)×G} t_P dW ≤ ε (the integrand is bounded, non-negative and supported in the compact set B_ρ(y) × G ⊆ O × G, on which W is finite, so the Bochner integral equals the lintegral used in (2)). Letting ρ ↓ 0 (HasTangentPlane W y T θ_y): θ_y∫ f_κ dv(T) = θ_y t_P(T) ∫_{T.plane} χ_κ(|z|) dH^n(z) ≤ ε, and ∫_{T.plane} χ_κ(|z|) dH^n ≥ H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = ω_nκ^n by 0(c). Hence t_P(T) ≤ ε/(θ_yω_nκ^n) ≤ ε/(ω_nκ^n); letting κ ↑ 1, t_P(T) ≤ ε/ω_n = L/4, so |Grassmannian.project T v − p v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for every v ∈ ℝ^N.

8. Graphs. By the tangent-graph-cover hypothesis (applied to N, n, L ∈ (0,1], the open set O, the varifold W and P) there are closed sets Γ_i (i ∈ ℕ) with |q(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for y, z ∈ Γ_i, such that every point x at which W has a tangent plane T (with some multiplicity) satisfying |Grassmannian.project T v − p v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v lies in some Γ_i. By step 7, G' ⊆ ⋃_i Γ_i.

9. Integer fibre bound. Let a ∈ P.plane with |a| < 1 and F_a := {y ∈ G' : p(y) = a}. Let s ⊆ F_a be finite. Each y ∈ s satisfies p(y) = a, y ∈ B_2(0), y ∈ spt μ, (1), (2), |y − p(y)| = |q(y)| < ε, HasDensity n μ y (ofReal θ̃(y)) and 1 ≤ ofReal θ̃(y). By allard_lemma (b) with x := a and Θ := fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ̃ y), and by 4(iv): Σ_{y∈s} θ̃(y) ≤ (1+δ)μ(B_1(a))/ω_n + δ ≤ (1+δ)(θ₀+δ) + δ < k₀ + 1. The left side is a sum of #s integers ≥ 1, so it is an integer ≤ k₀ and #s ≤ k₀. As every finite subset of F_a has at most k₀ elements, F_a is finite with #F_a ≤ k₀, and applying the bound to s := F_a gives Σ_{y∈F_a} θ̃(y) ≤ k₀; in [0,∞], the tsum over the finite fibre subtype equals this Finset sum, so Σ'_{y∈F_a} ofReal θ̃(y) ≤ k₀.

10. Mass estimate. Let χ_ε : ℝ → [0,1] be continuous with χ_ε = 1 on (−∞,ε/2] and χ_ε = 0 on [ε,∞), and g₀(y) := ψ(|p(y)|)χ_ε(|q(y)|). g₀ is continuous with compact support in {|p| ≤ 1/2, |q| ≤ ε} ⊆ B_2(0) ⊆ O, g₀(a) = ψ(|a|) for a ∈ P.plane (q = 0 there), and 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ ψ(|p|)·1_{{|p| < 1, |q| < ε}} ≤ 1. Using g₀ ≤ 1, step 6 with u := g₀·1_{ℝ^N ∖ E'} (Borel, vanishing off B_2(0)), the inclusion {|p| < 1, |q| < ε} ⊆ B_2(0), and the fact that (M̃ ∖ E') ∩ {|p| < 1, |q| < ε} differs from G' only by a subset of the H^n-null set Z:
 ∫ g₀ dμ ≤ μ(E') + ∫⁻_{ℝ^N∖E'} g₀ dμ ≤ c₀ε + ∫⁻_{(M̃ ∩ B_2(0))∖E'} g₀θ̃ dH^n ≤ c₀ε + ∫⁻_{G'} ofReal(ψ(|p(y)|)θ̃(y)) dH^n(y) (∫ g₀ dμ is a Bochner integral of a bounded compactly supported continuous function, equal to the corresponding lintegral).
 By the sibling graph_fibre_bound (with P, L, the Γ_i of step 8, G := G' and g(y) := ofReal(ψ(|p(y)|)θ̃(y))), the last integral is at most (1+L²)^{n/2}∫⁻_{P.plane} Σ_{y∈G', p(y)=a} ofReal(ψ(|p(y)|)θ̃(y)) dH^n(a) = (1+L²)^{n/2}∫⁻_{P.plane} ofReal(ψ(|a|))·Σ_{y∈F_a} ofReal θ̃(y) dH^n(a) ≤ (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀∫_{P.plane} ψ(|a|) dH^n(a) = (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀I₀, using step 9 when |a| < 1/2 and ψ(|a|) = 0 when |a| ≥ 1/2. Hence ∫ g₀ dμ_k ≤ c₀ε + (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀I₀ for all sufficiently large k.

11. Passage to the limit. By 0(b), ∫ g₀ dμ_k → θ₀∫_{P.plane} g₀ dH^n = θ₀I₀. Therefore θ₀I₀ ≤ c₀ε + (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀I₀, which is the claim of step 3.

12. Conclusion. The claim of step 3 holds for every sufficiently small δ > 0, with ε = δ⁴ → 0 and L = 4δ⁴/ω_n → 0 as δ → 0. Letting δ ↓ 0 gives θ₀I₀ ≤ k₀I₀, hence θ₀ ≤ k₀ because I₀ > 0, contradicting k₀ < θ₀. Hence θ₀ ∈ ℕ when n ≥ 1, and by step 1 also when n = 0: there is m ∈ ℕ with θ₀ = m. ∎
proof_key_steps: Portmanteau consequences of the convergence on B°_5(0); H^n of plane balls is ω_n s^n.
n = 0: weights are integer point-mass sums, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → θ₀, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ.
n ≥ 1, assume k₀ < θ₀ < k₀+1: for small δ, ε = δ⁴, L = 4ε/ω_n and large k, W_k satisfies (‡) of allard_lemma and μ_k(B_1(a)) ≤ (θ₀+δ)ω_n on the unit disc of P.
Bad set E with μ(E') ≤ c₀ε; canonical form of W_k (integral_density + canonical_representation), θ̃ ∈ ℕ_{≥1} H^n-a.e. on M̃.
Good tangent points have tilt ≤ ε/ω_n = L/4 by (2) and the tangent-plane limit; the graph cover puts them on closed L-graphs.
allard_lemma (b): every good fibre over |a| < 1 has θ̃-sum ≤ k₀.
graph_fibre_bound: ∫ g₀ dμ_k ≤ c₀ε + (1+L²)^{n/2}k₀I₀; letting k → ∞ then δ → 0 gives θ₀ ≤ k₀, a contradiction.

audit.reason: The proof handles dimension zero separately and correctly uses all declared dependencies and explicit sibling hypotheses. In positive dimension, integer good-fibre bounds and the graph inequality control good mass, while bad mass is bounded directly. Taking k→∞ and then δ→0 forces integer multiplicity without the printed concentration gap or circular reliance on compactness.
